list: Official 55-trophy list, as published by PlayStation and mirrored by Exophase and PSNProfiles, 18 November 2026
counts: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze; 28 hidden on PlayStation until earned
sources_note: Each trophy's name, description, grade and PSN progress target come from the official list as mirrored by Exophase and PSNProfiles (linked beside every guide). Every guide below is written for this entry, in my own words, from the official description; exact in-game spots and steps are not yet verified in play, and the guide says so where it matters. Hidden flags: PlayStation lists 28 of the 55 as hidden; this guide marks the story and secret ones (22) as hidden, since the exact hidden set is not published per trophy.
roadmap_note: Stage 1 story, stage 2 stranger strands and character finales, stage 3 activities and skills, stage 4 collectibles and exploration, stage 5 chaos, combat and money cleanup, then 100% completion and the platinum.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the finish line, not a task of its own: it pops the instant the other 54 trophies are earned. Follow the five roadmap stages in order — story, stranger strands, activities, collectibles, then the chaos and money cleanup — and this unlocks itself. If it has not popped after 54, re-check the tracker: one trophy is still unchecked. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the roadmap is my own plan built from the official descriptions.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.missable_reason: Tied to the opening mission Gone Fishing; a one-time story moment at the start of the game.
trophies.guide: Play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, to its end. It is the first mission of the game, so it unlocks naturally as you start the story — just follow the on-screen objectives until the mission-complete screen. Because it is the opening mission, you cannot come back to it later in the same playthrough if you somehow skip past it, so finish it before moving on. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the mission name and list; the warning is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1. Chapter trophies are unmissable in the normal sense: keep playing the story in order and the trophy pops at the chapter's final cutscene. Use the chapter as your first roadmap stage and clear its side content later — nothing in Chapter 1 needs to be done before the chapter ends. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the plan is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 2. Like the other chapter trophies, this one comes from playing the story through in order — no side task is needed for it. If you are hunting missables, Chapter 2 is where the first partner-based trophies can appear, so keep the Missables page open while you play this chapter. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the chapter plan is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 3. The trophy pops at the end of the chapter's final mission, so simply play the story in order. By this point the map is wide open, which makes it a good moment to start the long collectible counts (vehicles, WAiNK spots, meditation spots) between missions rather than leaving all of them for after the story. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the pacing advice is my own reading of the official descriptions.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 4, the last full chapter before the finale. The trophy pops when the chapter closes. Before you push into the final mission, pause and clear the missable trophies flagged in this guide — several partner and one-time moments live in the late story, and the finale may close them off. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the warning is my own reading of the official descriptions.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.missable_reason: The final mission closes the story; choices or moments inside it may not be replayable.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of the story. This is one of only two gold trophies, and it marks the end of the story arc. Do your missable cleanup BEFORE starting it: check the Missables page, finish the character finales and any partner trophies, and make a manual save first so you can reload if a choice inside the finale goes wrong. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the save-first advice is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.missable_reason: Tied to one named story mission, Breakfast Run; a single story moment.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. It unlocks as part of the story, so follow the mission markers until it appears and play it to completion. Named-mission trophies like this one are the reason to play the story in order and not skip cutscenes or objectives — the trophy is the mission itself. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the mission name and list; the advice is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.missable_reason: Tied to one named story mission, The Cartel Heist; a single story moment.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions are usually the longest set-pieces in the story, so take your time with the setup steps and follow the crew's instructions — the trophy pops when the heist itself is finished, not during the preparation. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the mission name and list; the advice is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.missable_reason: Tied to one named story mission, Child's Play; a single story moment.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. Play it when the story offers it and see it through to the mission-complete screen. If the mission offers a choice of approach, pick the one you are most comfortable executing — the trophy only asks that the mission is completed. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the mission name and list; the advice is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.missable_reason: Tied to one named story mission, Headliners; a single story moment.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. It is a named story mission, so it arrives in the story's normal order — follow the mission markers and finish it. Keep a manual save from before the mission in case a failed attempt locks you into a bad checkpoint; reloading a save is cheaper than replaying a chapter. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the mission name and list; the advice is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.missable_reason: Tied to one named story mission, VCIA Takedown; a single story moment at the airport.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set at Vice City International Airport. Finish the mission in full — the trophy is tied to completing it, not to any optional objective inside it. Do not confuse it with the free-roam airport trophy Catch Me If You Can; this one is the story mission itself. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the mission name and list; the distinction is my own reading of the two official descriptions.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.missable_reason: Tied to one named story mission, Operation Savage Glory; a single story moment.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. It is one of the late named missions, so it comes after most of the story — keep playing in order and it will appear. Stock up on armour and ammo before you start it, since late-story missions tend to be the hardest fights in the game. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the mission name and list; the preparation advice is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the in-game stats — the second gold trophy, and the real endgame of the platinum. PSN tracks this as a 0-to-100 counter. Everything in this guide feeds it: story, stranger strands, activities, collectibles and exploration. Check the game's completion checklist regularly; the last few percent are almost always a collectible set or an activity you have not tried. Do this last, after the other 53, and the platinum follows. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/100 PSN counter; the plan is my own reading of the official descriptions.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, near misses, drifts and airtime all count toward the PSN 0/250 counter. This is a grind trophy, not a skill gate: it accumulates across the whole playthrough, so drive fast, take ramps and jump gaps whenever you travel instead of fast-travelling. By the time the story is done you should be well past halfway; mop up the rest with a fast car and the stunt jumps scattered around Leonida. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/250 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once — PSN tracks this as a 0/9 counter, so one taste of each is enough. Work through the activity list in this guide (fishing, arcade, bowling, drone races, street races, shooting range, meditation, hunting and stunt-style activities) and tick each off as you try it; nothing needs to be won or completed, just attempted. Do this early so you learn which activities you enjoy before the long grinds. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/9 PSN counter; the activity list is my own reading of the official descriptions.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges — PSN tracks a 0/42 counter, and every single one must be gold, not just completed. This is the hardest silver in the list. Practice one weapon class at a time, learn each challenge's target pattern before going for gold, and use the range's retry freely: a failed run costs nothing but time. Save this for stage 3, after the story, when your aim and weapon handling are at their best. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/42 PSN counter; the approach is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations — PSN tracks a 0/14 counter, so every location needs its own win. Learn each course's line before racing for the win: fly the route once slowly to memorise the gates, then race it. The drones handle very differently from cars, so expect the first few locations to take several tries. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/14 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — PSN tracks a 0/20 counter, and the word different matters: replaying the same race does not add to it. Enter a fresh race each time, vary the vehicle class to match the course, and pick short circuits while you learn the racing lines. Street races unlock across Leonida as you explore, so combine this with the exploration trophy. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/20 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing challenges are head-to-head: land the better catch or the bigger haul than Cal within the challenge's rules. Watch the line tension and reel in steadily rather than yanking — most fishing losses come from snapping the line by reeling too hard. If you lose, challenge him again; there is no limit stated in the description. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the technique is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game, start to finish. Any arcade cabinet counts, so pick the shortest or easiest game in the arcade and play it through — you do not need a high score, just a completion. This is one of the quickest trophies in the list and a good first tick on the activities stage. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the advice is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.missable_reason: A character's final mission: once the strand closes, its finale cannot be replayed in the same playthrough.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Andy's strand. Stranger and contact strands work like mini-storylines: take Andy's missions whenever they appear on the map and keep going until his strand ends. Do not leave a strand half-finished while you rush the main story — finish Andy's finale before the final mission, in case the story's end closes side strands. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the warning is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.missable_reason: A character's final mission: once the strand closes, its finale cannot be replayed in the same playthrough.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Kenton's strand. Like Andy's, this is a contact storyline that ends with a finale mission — play Kenton's missions in order until the strand closes. The title hints at boats, so expect water in the finale and bring a fast boat or a good swim plan if the mission gives you the choice. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the warning is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.missable_reason: A character's final mission: once the strand closes, its finale cannot be replayed in the same playthrough.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Billy's strand. Play Billy's missions as they appear and see the strand through to its finale before you finish the main story. The name suggests a solo ride, so expect a bike or a long drive — keep a fast motorcycle handy when Billy calls. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the warning is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.missable_reason: Stranger strands appear at specific places and times; an unfinished strand may close when the story moves on.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida — PSN tracks a 0/8 counter, and a strand means the whole chain for one stranger, not a single mission. Strangers appear as map markers while you explore; talk to every one you meet and follow their chains to the end. This silver pairs with the five character finales: finish all the strands you find before the final mission, since the story's end may close them. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/8 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.missable_reason: A character's final mission: once the strand closes, its finale cannot be replayed in the same playthrough.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Randy's strand. Play Randy's missions in order until his storyline closes with its finale. Supply-and-demand work usually means moving goods between two points under pressure, so keep a fast, sturdy vehicle ready and expect a chase on the way back. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the warning is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.missable_reason: A character's final mission: once the strand closes, its finale cannot be replayed in the same playthrough.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Tyrone's strand. Work through Tyrone's missions as they appear and finish his finale before the story's final mission. The name points to spinning — a DJ, a turntable or a spin-out — so expect music or a vehicle stunt to feature in the finale, and play it when you are fresh rather than tired. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the warning is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida — PSN tracks a 0/18 counter. Meditation spots are quiet scenic places, usually on hills, beaches and lookouts; sit at each one and complete the meditation. This is a pure exploration trophy: fold it into the map-exploration stage and check spots off as you travel, rather than hunting all 18 in one trip. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/18 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.missable_reason: A unique animal for one character: if the hunt is tied to Bret's strand, it may close with it.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. This is a one-of-a-kind hunt, not regular hunting: follow Bret's instructions to track the animal, move slowly, and take the shot only when it is clean — a spooked unique animal may not come back. Do it as soon as Bret offers it, before his strand moves on. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the warning is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets — PSN tracks a 0/3 counter, and a set means every card in that set. Cards are scattered across Leonida in shops, houses and hidden spots; pick them up whenever you pass one rather than leaving them all for the end. Three sets is the requirement, so focus on the sets you are closest to finishing and trade or hunt down their last cards first. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/3 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It at 100 locations — PSN tracks a 0/100 counter, so this is the biggest location grind in the list. WAiNK spots are spread across the whole map, so the efficient way is to do it alongside the 52-area exploration trophy: every time you enter a new area, find its WAiNK spot before you leave. A hundred sounds like a lot, but it falls steadily if you tick spots off during normal travel instead of in one dedicated sweep. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/100 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges — PSN tracks a 0/50 counter across the game's challenge list. Challenges are the small goals layered over everything else (driving, shooting, exploring, activities), so they accumulate naturally while you chase the other trophies. If you stall near the end, open the challenge list and pick off the easiest unfinished ones: short driving or collection challenges first. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/50 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.missable_reason: Needs your partner beside you during a 4-star wanted level; partner availability is story-limited.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level and then lose it completely. Do it while your partner is available in free roam — commit crimes near a hiding spot, then break line of sight and stay out of the search area until the stars clear. The partner requirement is the tricky part: attempt it during a chapter where your partner roams with you, not after the story strands close. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the warning is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.missable_reason: Needs your partner beside you for three robberies in a row; partner availability is story-limited.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops back-to-back without ever losing your wanted level — the streak breaks if the stars clear between robberies. Plan a route of three close shops, hit them in quick succession, and keep moving: do not stop to fight the police, just drive to the next shop while the wanted level stays up. Attempt it while your partner is available in free roam. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the method and warning are my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles — PSN tracks a 0/100 counter, and discovering means getting into or registering a vehicle type you have not seen before. Variety is the whole game: drive everything you pass, from scooters to trucks to boats, instead of sticking to one favourite car. Rare vehicles hide in specific districts, so this pairs naturally with the 52-area exploration trophy. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/100 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during one single use of Combat Focus. Set it up deliberately: find a spot with at least five enemies close together, trigger Combat Focus, and work through them fast before it ends — do not waste it on one or two stragglers. A police shootout in a tight alley or a gang hideout gives you the crowd you need. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missable_reason: A one-time style stunt at the airport; easy to leave behind once you stop visiting VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at Vice City International Airport: get a plane off the ground without going through the normal departure routine. The clean way is to take a plane from the runway or a parked aircraft and lift off on your own terms, dodging airport security on the way in. Do it while you are already at VCIA for the story mission, so the trip is not wasted. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description is a joke about Rhinos — the tanks. Get inside a Rhino tank and put it to use: drive it, survive the wanted level it draws, and cause the chaos the trophy's humour points at. Tanks appear at military sites and at high wanted levels, so the practical route is to reach a 4- or 5-star wanted level near a base and take one. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the reading of the joke and the method are my own, from the official description.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.missable_reason: A stealth robbery with a strict no-detection condition; a failed loud attempt may close the clean window.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — no alarms, no witnesses, no wanted level. Plan it like a stealth mission: case the store, enter quietly, take the goods and leave before anyone reacts. If you are spotted, the attempt fails, so reload a manual save made just before you walk in rather than trying to salvage a loud robbery. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape each time — PSN tracks a 0/5 counter, and the escape is part of the requirement, not just the robbery. Plan every vault with its getaway in mind: a fast car parked close, a route out of the search area, and no lingering to fight police. Five vaults means five clean getaways, so treat the escape as the real trophy. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/5 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida — intercept one, stop it, crack it open and get clear before the police box you in. The escape matters as much as the robbery, so have your getaway car ready before you start, not after. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida — PSN tracks a 0/52 counter, one tick per named area you set foot in. This is the backbone of the collectible stage: drive, fly and sail through every district, island and backroad until the counter reads 52. Combine it with the WAiNK spots, meditation spots and vehicle discoveries in the same trips so no journey is wasted. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/52 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs — PSN tracks a 0/9 counter, one per gang. Each gang runs its own operations in its own territory, so work through the map gang by gang and tick them off; the tracker in this guide shows which count you have. Expect a fight at every operation, so go in armed and with an escape route. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/9 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.missable_reason: A specific quiet moment at a specific place; easy to walk past and never return to.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Head to a bar or beachfront spot on Ocean Beach with a view of the water, order a cocktail and take it in — the trophy is about the moment, not a challenge. Do it early in a play session as a breather between harder trophies; it is one of the gentlest ticks on the whole list. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.missable_reason: A one-time stunt in a showroom; once smashed, the moment may not repeat cleanly.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style: drive a car straight through the showroom glass and out the front. Pick a fast car, line up on the showroom's glass front, and floor it — the 'classic style' is the old-school drive-through-the-window exit. Make a manual save before you try, in case the first attempt ends in a wreck instead of an exit. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley: go to that specific alley, pick up a ball and bowl. 'Follow-through' points at the bowling action itself, so play a full frame or game rather than just walking in. This is a quick, low-pressure trophy — pair it with the arcade visit in the same activities session. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.missable_reason: A partnership moment tied to the story's duo; may only be available while the partnership is active.
trophies.guide: The description is deliberately vague — 'a partnership with mass appeal' — which means it is a story moment for the game's central duo, likely tied to something the pair does that the public notices. Play the story with your partner, take part in the duo's big public moments, and it should pop on its own. If it has not popped by the finale, check the story beats you may have rushed past. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the reading is my own, from the official description alone — the exact trigger is not yet verified in play.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.missable_reason: PSN tracks choices up to 500; choices are one-time story decisions that cannot be remade in the same playthrough.
trophies.guide: PSN tracks choices up to 500 for this trophy — every meaningful decision you make in the story and in side content counts toward it. There is no shortcut: make choices whenever the game offers them, in missions, stranger strands and activities, and the counter climbs across the playthrough. Because choices are one-time, this is flagged missable — a skipped decision is a skipped tick, so always choose rather than walking away from a choice. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/500 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.missable_reason: Needs a failure followed by a success on the second try; a first-try success may close the window.
trophies.guide: 'Second time's the charm' means exactly what it says: fail something once, then succeed on the second attempt. The practical reading is a mission or challenge you fail and then pass on the retry — so if you fail a mission, do not reload an old save to erase the failure; retry it from the checkpoint and finish it. If you pass everything first time, deliberately attempt something hard, fail once, and then complete it on the second go. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.missable_reason: A strange one-off event somewhere in Leonida; miss it and you may never see it again in that playthrough.
trophies.guide: 'What the hell just happened?' is the game's nod to a strange, unexplainable event — the classic GTA easter egg trophy. Explore odd corners of the map, visit strange landmarks at night, and investigate anything that looks out of place; the trophy pops when you witness the event. It is flagged missable because a one-off event can be walked past — if you hear about a weird sighting, go and see it right away. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the reading is my own, from the official description alone — the exact event is not yet verified in play.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl someone over with a melee drive-by: swing a melee weapon from a moving vehicle and knock a pedestrian down like a bowling pin. Drive slowly past a pedestrian, lean out and swing — speed makes the aim harder, so a slow roll is better than a fast pass. Pick a quiet street so you are not fighting traffic while you line it up. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the official list; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts — PSN tracks a 0/250,000 counter. Marked Bills come from robberies and heists, and your contacts turn them into clean cash; keep feeding bills to contacts whenever you have them instead of letting them pile up. This accumulates across the whole playthrough, so start laundering early and it will be done by the cleanup stage. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/250,000 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — PSN tracks a 0/100,000 counter, and every shop counts: clothes, weapons, food, car mods. The money you launder for the Marked Bills trophy is the money you spend here, so the two trophies feed each other. Buy gear you actually want as you play rather than hoarding cash, and the counter will be finished by the time the story ends. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/100,000 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties — PSN tracks a 0/8 counter. Garages are bought with the clean cash from your laundering, and each one gives you somewhere to store the vehicles you discover for the 100-vehicle trophy, so the two trophies pair well. Buy a garage whenever you can afford one rather than saving up for all eight at once. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/8 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — PSN tracks a 0/10 counter. Open the Scooter Bros app on your in-game phone, pick a vehicle you own or have found, and register it; repeat with ten different vehicles. This pairs with the 100-vehicle discovery trophy: every new vehicle you find is a candidate for registration. Sources: Exophase and PSNProfiles for the 0/10 PSN counter; the method is my own reading of the official description.
